questions.question: Does DirectMessageNotificationsWatcher.tsx's new mount+interval effect genuinely call the real runInviteExpiryCycle export (not a locally re-implemented copy, not a no-op stand-in that only logs), and does the accompanying unit test assert the real function was invoked with real fake-timer advancement, not a spy that always resolves regardless of whether the interval fired?

Does the new effect in the sweep host call runInviteExpiryCycle through inviteExpirySweep.ts's existing exported entry point (the declared seam), with no inline reimplementation of the migrate/sweep/derive steps inside DirectMessageNotificationsWatcher.tsx itself?

Could `sweep host` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md?

Does app/tests/unit/marmot/directMessageNotificationsWatcherSweep.test.ts use vi.useFakeTimers (no jsdom, per project convention) to assert runInviteExpiryCycle fires once on mount AND again after each subsequent 60-second tick for multiple ticks, and does the test genuinely FAIL if the interval registration is deleted or the tick duration is changed — i.e. is it load-bearing, not a tautological assertion that passes regardless of the interval's presence?

Per spec.md's TRAP 1 mandatory fix and architecture.md's note that the cycle is 'already idempotent/double-mount-safe,' does the sweep host's new copy of the effect coexist safely with NotificationBell.tsx's still-live copy during the interim (both call the same idempotent cycle, no double-counting of a single expiry, no conflicting IDB writes) — and is this coexistence actually exercised by a test, or only asserted in prose?

Does the new interval effect clear its interval (clearInterval / effect cleanup) on unmount of DirectMessageNotificationsWatcher.tsx, so the sweep host cannot leak a running interval past the component's lifecycle?

For AC-SWEEP-1 (on mount of the sweep host, runInviteExpiryCycle MUST fire at least once, independently of NotificationBell.tsx): show (a) the mount effect's production code, (b) a test asserting the real function is called on mount with no bell component present in the test, and (c) confirmation this is not a mock-spy proxy that only checks a call count without confirming which function was called.

For AC-SWEEP-2 (after mount, runInviteExpiryCycle MUST continue firing on a 60-second interval for as long as the host remains mounted, and a controllable-clock test MUST fail if the interval is removed or the host unmounted without replacement): show (a) the interval registration code, (b) the fake-timer test advancing multiple 60s ticks and asserting call count increments each time, and (c) evidence the test was run against a deliberately-broken variant (interval removed) and observed to fail, confirming it is state-discriminating rather than a false-green.
